evidence.supports: s6, 'When the ruler changed': how the Nielsen People Meter measured the audience
evidence.statement: The Nielsen People Meter, adopted as the national US television-audience standard in September 1987, had a button for each member of the sampled household, preprogrammed with that person's sex and age. Each person was supposed to press their button whenever they turned the set on or off, or came into or left the room. It replaced a paper diary that a household member filled in by hand at the end of each day or week. Nielsen argued the People Meter was more accurate than the diary method.

sources.name: Christian Science Monitor, 'For TV networks, People Meter is a profit eater', 6 January 1988
